title: The Broken Choir
premise: Yara Eriksen, the last of the oath-bound swordspeakers whose voices can unmake steel and memory alike, has spent a decade hiding among the smugglers' roads of the Thornfell mountains. When the crown's Inquisitor-General launches a hunt for the gifted, Yara is forced to shelter a fugitive child who carries the sealed memory of the Choir—the ancient order whose fall sparked a war that nearly ended the world. As Yara uncovers that the crown itself was built on a stolen song, they must choose between staying invisible and speaking the truth that could either free the realm or reignite the old war. In the end, Yara breaks their oath to sing the whole memory aloud, shattering the crown's legitimacy but scattering the gift into ordinary people, ending the age of chosen wielders forever.
about_author: Ada Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing suppressed folk songs in mountain villages before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about memory, justice, and the people history tries to forget.

chapters.title: Salt on the Pass
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A routine smuggling run through Thornfell establishes Yara's mastery of hidden roads and their careful silence about the gift. When they quietly unbind a seized wagon with a whispered word, the emotional beat is the loneliness of a power that must never be used.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the market town of Greyhollow, criers announce the Crown Hunt: all swordspeakers to be registered or killed. Yara watches an old woman dragged away for humming a forbidden cadence, feeling guilt curdle into fear.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Remembers
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Retreating to a cave shrine, Yara performs a private rite of remembrance for the dead Choir, revealing through flashback how they survived the purge ten years ago while their mentor burned.

chapters.title: The Child in the Snow
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On a frozen pass, Yara finds Merrin, an eight-year-old fugitive with a seal scar over her heart and no memory of her name. The beat is reluctant compassion overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: Inquisitor-General Vael
chapters.summary: Vael's POV. The antagonist arrives in Greyhollow, charming and methodical, interrogating prisoners with a device that extracts sung memories. We learn he hunts not to destroy the gift but to harvest it.

chapters.title: A Debt in Lowmarsh
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Seeking help from Brannoc, an ex-Choir healer turned drunk, Yara trades a dangerous favor for Merrin's concealment. Emotional beat: the cost of old friendships strained by old betrayals.

chapters.title: The Seal Scar
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Examining Merrin, Brannoc recognizes the work of the Last Cantor and realizes the girl carries a sealed fragment of the Choir's founding memory—a truth that could topple thrones.

chapters.title: Hounds of Quiet
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The Hunt's scent-hounds, deaf men trained to feel resonance, track Merrin. A night chase through the marshes ends with Yara killing for the first time in a decade, and hating how easily it returns.

chapters.title: Oath and Ash
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. By firelight, Yara explains the swordspeaker's oath—power bound to restraint—to Merrin, who asks the devastating question: 'Who made you promise?' The beat is doubt taking root.

chapters.title: The Gilded Choir Loft
chapters.summary: Vael's POV. In the capital, Vael reports to Chancellor Ives, revealing the crown has been singing a stolen sustaining hymn for two centuries—and it is failing. Power's rot shown from inside.

chapters.title: Road of Nine Bends
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A tense journey through smuggler territory where Yara must bargain with the Ferrywoman, a fence of secrets who offers passage in exchange for one true memory. Yara pays with a lie instead.

chapters.title: Merrin Dreams in Old Tongue
chapters.summary: Merrin's POV. First chapter in the child's voice: dreams of towers and ten thousand voices, waking words she doesn't know she knows. The beat is eerie wonder and Yara's dawning dread.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse Trap
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Ambushed at a tollhouse by Hunt riders, Yara uses the gift openly for the first time, unmaking a squad's weapons. Witnesses see. Invisibility is over; the beat is exhilaration followed by horror.

chapters.title: Wanted: The Last Speaker
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs via broadside excerpts and town gossip. Yara's face spreads across the mountains with a bounty. Brannoc is arrested as bait. The net tightens.

chapters.title: The Ferrywoman's Price Called Due
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The Ferrywoman reveals she knew Yara lied and now demands the real payment—or Merrin. Yara refuses, burning a bridge (literally) and losing their last neutral ally.

chapters.title: What Brannoc Sang Under the Knife
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Interrogated by Vael, Brannoc resists the memory-extraction, then deliberately feeds him a false memory to protect Yara. The beat is sacrifice disguised as defeat.

chapters.title: The Hollow Abbey
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara and Merrin shelter in the ruined abbey where the Choir fell. Among the scorched pews, Merrin's seal begins to crack, leaking fragments: the crown's hymn was stolen from the Choir's founding song.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Years of Borrowed Breath
chapters.summary: Vael's POV. Vael confronts Chancellor Ives with evidence the sustaining hymn fails within a year. Ives orders Merrin captured alive at any cost. Vael begins privately questioning whom he serves.

chapters.title: The Smugglers' Parliament
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara appeals to the smuggler clans for protection, offering roads and gold. Half refuse; the Kestrel clan agrees—for a price yet unnamed. Beat: uneasy alliance, community forming around the hunted.

chapters.title: Cracks in the Seal
chapters.summary: Merrin's POV. Merrin's memories surface in waking life now—she hums harmonies that mend broken tools, frighten horses, stop arguments mid-word. She is becoming a vessel whether anyone chooses it or not.

chapters.title: The Kestrel's Price
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Clan-mother Sera Kestrel names her price: when the truth comes out, Yara must speak it publicly, in the capital, under their own name—not vanish afterward. Yara cannot promise. The beat is being asked to be brave before ready.

chapters.title: Winter March
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The party moves toward the capital through blizzard and pursuit. A quiet chapter of bonds deepening: Merrin teaching Yara a children's round, Yara admitting fear aloud for the first time.

chapters.title: Vael's Doubt
chapters.summary: Vael's POV. Extracting Brannoc's false memory, Vael experiences a forged vision of the Choir's fall so beautiful it shakes his certainty. He begins his own secret investigation into the crown's hymn.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Coldspring
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A set-piece battle: Hunt forces corner them at a river bridge. Sera's clan arrives unexpectedly, honoring the debt early. Victory, but Merrin is grazed by a resonance-tipped arrow and the seal fractures badly.

chapters.title: What Leaks Through
chapters.summary: Merrin's POV. Feverish, Merrin relives the founding of the Choir in full sensory memory—and the reader learns the war's true origin: the first king stole the song and murdered the singers to own it alone.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Shrine
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the mountain shrine, Yara faces the core dilemma: keep Merrin hidden and let the crown's hymn fail into chaos, or carry her to the capital and risk everything on truth. Yara chooses the road to the city.

chapters.title: Entry into Greyfall
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Disguised as pilgrims, they enter the capital during the Hymnal Festival, when the stolen song is sung publicly. Yara hears its hollowness firsthand—the realm's foundation audibly fraying.

chapters.title: Prison of Glass
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Held in the resonance cells beneath the palace, Brannoc discovers other surviving speakers, including someone from Yara's past thought dead. Hope rekindles in the dark.

chapters.title: The Festival of False Song
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. During the festival climax, the sustaining hymn stutters publicly for the first time in living memory. Panic seeds through the crowd. Vael watches the Chancellor lie smoothly and makes his decision.

chapters.title: Bargain with the Turncoat
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Vael finds Yara first—not to arrest them, but to propose alliance: he will open the prison if Yara swears the truth spoken will include his name among the deceived, not the guilty. Distrustful truce.

chapters.title: Descent Beneath the Palace
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The infiltration chapter: smuggler routes mapped onto palace drains, Vael's keys, near-discoveries. The beat is breathless tension and Yara confronting the architecture of the lie itself.

chapters.title: The Cells Where Voices Go
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Reunion with Brannoc and the imprisoned speakers—but freeing them triggers the alarm. Sera's clan creates diversionary fires across the city. Loyalties pay their debts in flame.

chapters.title: Ives Unmasked
chapters.summary: Chancellor Ives's POV. Cornered, Ives reveals his true plan: rather than let the hymn fail, he will bind Merrin permanently to the throne as a living engine, a child sacrificed to continuity. Pure corruption of power.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Oath
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Climax begins: to stop the binding rite, Yara must break their oath and speak with full, unbound voice—risking the same madness that destroyed the old Choir. They choose to sing.

chapters.title: The Whole Memory
chapters.summary: Merrin's POV. Climax peak: Merrin willingly opens her seal, and together she and Yara sing the complete founding memory into every mind in Greyfall. The stolen hymn collapses; the crowd remembers everything at once.

chapters.title: When the Crowd Remembered
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The city erupts—not into war, but into grief and refusal. Soldiers lower weapons as shared memory dissolves the enemy. Ives falls to his own guards' remembered consciences. Vael stands aside.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Throne
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Aftermath in the shattered palace: no clean victory. The realm has no government, the gift is destabilizing, and Yara's voice is damaged from the unbinding. The cost is counted honestly.

chapters.title: Scattering the Song
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. With Brannoc and the freed speakers, Yara performs the Dissolution: the gift released into thousands of ordinary voices, weak alone, strong in chorus. No more chosen ones; only neighbors.

chapters.title: The Long Road Down
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara walks Merrin home to the family she barely remembers, then keeps walking. Quiet, elegiac chapter about what justice costs the one who carries it.

chapters.title: First Voice of the New Choir
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Merrin's POV. A year later, in a rebuilt Greyhollow, villagers sing a harvest round and their small gifts flicker harmlessly among them. Merrin, apprenticed to Brannoc, hears on the wind a familiar voice on a far pass—Yara, still walking, still free. Hope without certainty closes the book.
